summary: Herman Tull is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Edwin Gerow and Wendy Doniger. He held a post at Balliol College, Oxford (attested 2013).

Hermann Ammann was a linguist who studied at Freiburg (Ph.D. 1910) under Rudolf Thurneysen and at Heidelberg. He worked at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae (1911–1913), the University of Freiburg (1920, 1926), and the University of Innsbruck (1928).

Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg Huth and Richard Pischel, earning his Ph.D. at Berlin, and held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin, Berlin University (1910–1921), and Stuttgart's Priesterseminar (~1928–1937).

Hermann Berger was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Munich studying under Helmut Hoffmann, Ferdinand Sommer, Karl Hoffmann, and Anton Scherer. He served as Privatdozent at Munich and Dean at Heidelberg University (1964–1993).

Hermann Beythan, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission and under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai. He served as Lecturer in Tamil at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1933–1945).

Hermann Bonitz was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg. He served at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1867–1888).

Hermann Brockhaus, an Indologist and linguist, earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig and studied at Göttingen and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel and Christian Lassen. He was a professor at Jena (1839–1841) and Leipzig (from 1841 until 1877).

Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Bonn, Berlin, and Zurich (Ph.D.) under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (1873–1888), Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901), and the University of Bern (1901–1914).

Hermann Camillo Kellner worked in Indology and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus and Georg Curtius. He taught at the Thomasschule zu Leipzig (~1866–1907) and Gymnasium Zwickau (1887).

Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen under August Fick, Theodor Benfey, and others. He was a professor at Bryn Mawr (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).
Hermann Diels, who worked in philosophy and history/archaeology, studied at Berlin and Bonn under Hermann Usener. He held a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1882 to 1922.
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from ~1875 to 1879. He served as a professor at the University of Giessen from ~1893 to 1922.

Hermann Ethé was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and Indology who studied at Greifswald, Leipzig (Ph.D.), Munich, and Oxford. He catalogued manuscripts at the Bodleian Library (1872) and became Professor of Oriental Languages at Aberystwyth (1875).

Hermann Friedrich Mögling was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1829–1834) and the Basel Mission (1834). He served as a teacher and preacher with the Basel Mission from 1838 to 1852.

Hermann Fränkel studied at Berlin under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff, as well as at Bonn and Göttingen. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1920–1935) and Stanford University (~1935–1953).

Hermann Goetz worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Munich and being mentored by Jean Philippe Vogel. He was curator at the Baroda Museum (1939–1953) and directed art history at Heidelberg University (1961–1976).

Hermann Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher and August Boeckh, and later taught at the Ottoschule Stettin, Friedrich-Wilhelms-Schule Stettin, and Marienstiftsgymnasium, where he was made professor in 1852.

Hermann Gundert, an Indologist and linguist, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen (~1831–1835). He served with the Church Missionary Society (~1835–1838), the Basel Mission (1838), and headed Calwer Verlag from 1860.

Hermann Güntert, a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies, earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff and Christian Bartholomae. He held professorships at the University of Rostock (1921) and Heidelberg University (1926–1945).

Hermann Hirt, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Freiburg and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and others. He served as Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891–1912) and ordinary professor of Sanskrit and Comparative IE at Giessen (1912–1936).
